newsitem.title: GERMANY: More ad spending equals more sales - German study.
newsitem.headline: More ad spending equals more sales - German study.

text.p: A study of brand-name products in Germany has shown a direct relationship between the amount of money a company spends on ads and its success on the market.
"The higher the media budget of a brand name is, the more successful it is," the MediaGruppe Muenchen, a media marketing firm, said in a summary of study data released last week.
"This relationship applies to the whole advertising budget as well as just to spending on television ads."

Researchers monitored about 270 brand-name products over a three-year period and measured success by increases in market share during half-year intervals, MGM said. Nearly 47 percent of the products were considered "successful".
It added that breaks in a company's ad strategy, in which spots were introduced to the media and then taken away for a time, were particularly detrimental to a brand-name product.
Data indicated a company was better off with continuous ads that did not run as frequently than in producing short but intensive ad spurts, MGM said.
The study also identified a negative influence of price-cutting on a brand's market share.

"Price-cutting is counterproductive for the success of a brand name," MGM said. It added that losses in turnover due to lower prices were not able to be replaced entirely by increasing ad spending either, despite the sales ads boost.
Product innovation, however, did prove to boost a product's chances for success and was compounded when combined with higher ad investment, MGM said.
